<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par69 />{{GHGmargin-letter|69|d}}
In more than half the number of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} the original {{GHGterm|Wāw}} in the above-mentioned forms gives place to {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}, which, unless it suffers aphaeresis (see f), appears:—

in the ''imperatives'' {{GHGheb|text=יְצֹק}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְרַשׁ}} and ''infinitives'' {{GHGheb|text=יְסֹד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְרֹא}}, as a strong consonant, but

in the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִירַשׁ}}, properly ''yiyrăš'', merges with the preceding ''ĭ'' into ''î''.

In the second syllable ''imperfects'' of this form regularly have ''ă''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|e}}
(''a'') That the latter forms are derived from verbs with an original {{GHGterm|Wāw}} (not {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}) is shown partly by the inflexion of these verbs in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} (where the original {{GHGterm|Wāw}} reappears throughout), and partly by the Arabic, in which verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}} likewise exhibit a twofold formation; cf. ''wălădă'', imperf. ''yălĭdu'', with elision of the {{GHGterm|Wāw}}, and ''wăǵĭlă, yauǵalu'', with retention of the {{GHGterm|Wāw}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|f}}
(''b'') Sometimes both forms, the weaker and the stronger, occur in the same verb; cf. {{GHGheb|text=צַק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=41}} and {{GHGheb|text=יְצֹק|translate=pour}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=3}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=יִֽצְקוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=34}} and the ''infin.'' {{GHGheb|text=צֶ֫קֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=38|verse=27}}); {{GHGheb|text=רֵשׁ|translate=take possession}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=15}} (but cf. s), {{GHGheb|text=רָשׁ}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} for {{GHGheb|text=רַשׁ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=24.31}}; ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=רְשׁוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=23|hidebook=1}}, but also, with {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} {{GHGterm|paragogic}}, {{GHGheb|text=יְרָ֫שָׁה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=23}}. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִיקַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=22}} and {{GHGheb|text=יֵקַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=16}} ''it shall be kindled''; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּיקַר|translate=it was precious}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=30}} and {{GHGheb|text=יֵקַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=9}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=יֵיקַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=72|verse=14}}).—The form {{GHGheb|text=וַֽיֱּחֶמוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=39}}, for {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּֽחֲמוּ}}, beside {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּחַ֫מְנָה}} verse 38, is remarkable; cf. {{GHGpar|47|k}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|g}}
(''c'') On {{GHGheb|text=רַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=11}} for {{GHGheb|text=יְרַד}} and {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=42|verse=10}} for the {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} {{GHGheb|text=יָשׁוֹב}}, cf. {{GHGpar|19|i}}.—But {{GHGheb|text=יְרַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=13}} (twice) is not intended by the Masora either as {{GHGterm|perfect}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יָרַד}}, which really should be restored) or as {{GHGterm|imperative}} of {{GHGheb|text=יָרַד}}, but as an apocopated {{GHGterm|imperfect Piʿēl}} from {{GHGheb|text=רָדָה}} (={{GHGheb|text=יְרַדֶּה}}) ''to have dominion''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|h}}
(''d'') The eight verbs,<ref>A ninth {{GHGheb|text=יָסַף|translate=to add}}, is also to be included. In the ''Mêšaʿ''-inscription, l. 21, the {{GHGterm|infinitive}} is written {{GHGheb|text=לספת}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=יספתי}}, l. 29); hence read in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=1}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=29|verse=18}}) {{GHGheb|text=סֶ֫פֶת}} for {{GHGheb|text=סְפוֹת}}. The 2nd ''plur. masc. imperative'' {{GHGheb|text=סְפוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=21}} corresponds to {{GHGheb|text=שְׁבוּ}}; thus in proof of a supposed {{GHGheb|text=סָפָה|translate=addere}}, there remains only {{GHGheb|text=אַסְפֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=23}}, for which, according to {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=8}}, read {{GHGheb|text=אֹסִ֫פָה}}.</ref> of which the initial consonant in the above-mentioned forms always suffers elision or aphaeresis, are {{GHGheb|text=יָלַד|translate=to bring forth}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָצָא|translate=to go forth}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשַׁב|translate=to sit, to dwell}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָרַד|translate=to descend}}, also {{GHGheb|text=הָלַךְ|translate=to go}} (cf. below, x); and with ''ă'' in the second syllable of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָדַע|translate=to know}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָחַד|translate=to be united}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָקַע|translate=to be dislocated}}. Examples of the other formation ({{GHGheb|text=יִירַשׁ}}, &c.) are {{GHGheb|text=יָעֵף|translate=to be wearied}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָעַץ|translate=to counsel}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשֵׁן|translate=to sleep}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָרֵא}} ({{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִירָא}}, {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=יְרָא}}) ''to fear''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|i}}
'''2.''' The original {{GHGterm|Wāw}} is retained as a firm consonant: (''a'') in the ''infinitive, imperative'', and {{GHGterm|imperfect Niphʿal}}, being protected by the strengthening, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִוָּשֵׁב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִוָּשֵׁב}}, which are consequently strong forms like {{GHGheb|text=הִקָּטֵל}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִקָּטֵל}}; (''b'') in the ''Hithpaʿel'' of some verbs, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִתְוַדַּע}} from {{GHGheb|text=יָדַע}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְוַכַּח}} from {{GHGheb|text=יָכַח}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִתְוַדָּה}} from {{GHGheb|text=יָדָה}}; otherwise a radical {{GHGterm|Wāw}} at the beginning of a word is now found only in a few nouns, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וָלָד|translate=offspring}} from {{GHGheb|text=יָלַד|translate=to bear}}.
